difficultyReason: Three straightforward facts with one clear hedged inference. A study found a specific correlation; correct answer draws a modest conclusion about what tends to occur. Distractors overreach or are irrelevant.
stimulus: A pharmaceutical study followed 300 patients with moderate arthritis over 12 months. Those who took a new anti-inflammatory medication reported pain reduction within two weeks. Patients who took the medication consistently for at least eight weeks showed sustained improvement in mobility. The study found no serious side effects in any participant.
questionStem: Which one of the following is most strongly supported by the information above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The new anti-inflammatory medication will eliminate arthritis pain in all patients who take it.

choices.label: B
choices.text: At least some patients with moderate arthritis may experience sustained improvement in mobility from consistent use of the medication.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Patients who take the medication for less than eight weeks will not benefit from it.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The medication is safer than all other arthritis treatments currently available.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pain reduction is the most important symptom to address in arthritis treatment.

explanations.correct: The stimulus states that patients who took the medication consistently for at least eight weeks showed sustained improvement. This directly supports that at least some patients (those in the study) experienced this benefit. The answer uses appropriate hedging ('may experience') and respects the scope of the data.
explanations.A: Too strong — the stimulus says patients 'reported pain reduction,' not that it will eliminate pain. Also says 'no serious side effects,' not that it is entirely safe or effective for all.
explanations.C: Too strong — the stimulus does not say that patients taking it for less than eight weeks will not benefit. Some may still benefit; the study only notes what happened with those who took it for at least eight weeks.
explanations.D: Unsupported scope creep — the stimulus compares only to a control or baseline within the study, not to 'all other arthritis treatments.'
explanations.E: Plausible but unsupported — the stimulus never argues that pain reduction is the most important symptom relative to mobility.

difficultyReason: Three related facts about linguistic patterns in a specific region. Clear factual basis for a modest inference about how speakers in that region tend to use language. Distractors either overreach to absolute claims or apply the finding beyond the stated scope.
stimulus: A linguistic survey of 450 speakers in northern coastal towns found that roughly 80 percent of those speakers use a distinctive pronunciation of the vowel in words like 'bath' and 'path.' In the same towns, approximately 75 percent of speakers aged 18 to 35 use this pronunciation, as do approximately 85 percent of speakers over age 50. The pronunciation has remained stable across these age groups for at least two decades.
questionStem: The statements above, if true, most strongly support which one of the following claims?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All speakers in northern coastal towns pronounce 'bath' and 'path' with the distinctive vowel sound.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The distinctive pronunciation is found in fewer than half of all English speakers.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Speakers over age 50 in northern coastal towns are more likely than younger speakers to use the distinctive pronunciation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The distinctive pronunciation will eventually disappear from northern coastal towns.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Linguistic features that remain stable for two decades will never change.

explanations.correct: The stimulus directly states that approximately 85 percent of speakers over age 50 use the pronunciation, while approximately 75 percent of speakers aged 18 to 35 use it. This supports the claim that speakers over 50 are more likely (by about 10 percentage points) to use the pronunciation than younger speakers.
explanations.A: Too strong — the stimulus says roughly 80 percent use the pronunciation, not all.
explanations.B: Unsupported scope creep — the stimulus concerns only speakers in northern coastal towns, not English speakers generally.
explanations.D: Opposite direction — the stimulus says the pronunciation has remained stable, not that it will disappear.
explanations.E: Too strong — stability over two decades does not entail that something will never change.
